propositions: _lib_writes.py is at the 800-line hard cap enforced by CI module-size gate, blocking new features like optional create_ticket arguments from landing
The module aggregates seven distinct concerns (genesis, identity/keys, status lifecycle, leaf mutations, session logs, store maintenance, signing) that should be separated to enable future growth

A two-cut refactoring splits concerns into _lib_mutations.py (mutations, logs, store ops) and _lib_identity.py (identity, key material, signing) while keeping _lib_writes.py (genesis, status lifecycle)
All 27 public names must remain re-exported from _lib_writes and accessible via rebar.<name> and rebar._lib_writes.<name> facades without modifying __init__.py or _lib_gates.py
The split preserves byte-identical function bodies (behavior-preserving refactor) with no logic rewritten, verified by reconstructing pre-split blocks from new files
